narrative:
The model determined that you have a 25% chance of being a bad credit risk. While this is not an extremely high probability, it was enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

The three factors that mattered most in this decision were the length of the loan you requested, the purpose of the loan, and the status of your checking account. 

Your short nine-month loan request actually worked in your favor and pushed the prediction toward approval, as approved applicants typically ask for almost twice as long (19 months on average). Unfortunately, two other important factors pulled the decision in the opposite direction. The fact that you want the money for business purposes made the bank more cautious; only 9% of approved applicants use loans for business compared with far more common uses like buying a radio or TV. Your checking account balance between 0 and 200 DM also increased the risk in the model's view, since most approved applicants either have no checking account or maintain higher balances.

Because the negative influences from the loan purpose and account status outweighed the positive effect of the short duration, the overall prediction tipped against approval.

You should focus on building a stronger checking account balance and perhaps consider a loan for a more common purpose. Reapplying in a few months with these improvements could lead to a better outcome. (218 words)
